instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and survey responses, then respond ONLY with a valid JSON object containing maturity_score, opportunities, next_steps, and key_weaknesses.

answers.companyDescription: Pulse Partners is a mental health tech company providing an app-based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) program complemented by human therapist chat support, serving 18,000 active users. We leverage robust clinical evidence from published Randomized Controlled Trials to validate efficacy, which has established strong brand trust within the therapeutic community and corporate wellness channels.
answers.pastInitiatives: Innovation is currently unstructured; efforts are sporadic and function as ad-hoc experiments driven by individual team enthusiasm rather than a formalized pipeline. These initiatives often lack executive sponsorship, standardized metrics, or dedicated budget allocation, leading to high variability in execution.
answers.strategicGoals: The board has mandated that 25% of revenue must originate from entirely new products or services not present in the current portfolio within three years. This requires systematic exploration into adjacent markets and alternative monetization models, balancing organic build initiatives with strategic acquisitions.
answers.teamSize: Our R&D function consists of 10-12 engineers organized into two squads focused on core product innovation and exploratory business model prototyping, supported by two data engineers building our analytics infrastructure. Innovation projects follow a lean startup methodology with clear go/no-go criteria at 3-month checkpoints.
answers.additionalContext: The organization operates in a low-regulation environment that allows for agile iteration but requires careful management to ensure clinical compliance remains paramount as we expand services.

opportunities.title: Corporate Wellness Platform Integration
opportunities.rationale: Given the existing corporate wellness pilot interest and low risk profile, developing tiered modules for executive coaching or specialized stress management tools represents a low-risk incremental revenue stream. This leverages current user data without requiring massive R&D expenditure.

first_actions: Pilot development of one premium corporate wellness module
Define KPIs for adoption and retention within the existing 6 months
execution_plan.success_metric: Achieve 50 paying corporate clients in Q3 with an average LTV of $X
milestones: M1: Module MVP launch and pilot in Q2
M2: Successful integration into three major corporate wellness contracts by M4

opportunities.title: Target Acquisition of Adjacent Wellness Tech
opportunities.rationale: To meet the 25% diversification goal, acquiring a small, specialized health platform focused on preventative care or chronic disease management provides rapid market entry into a new segment. This allows Pulse Partners to bypass long organic development cycles.

first_actions: Identify three potential acquisition targets matching the 'preventative care' profile
Establish an M&A due diligence framework aligned with conservative risk appetite
execution_plan.success_metric: Successful acquisition of a target resulting in $5M ARR within 12 months
milestones: M1: Target identification and initial pitch deck by M2
M2: Due diligence completion and offer acceptance by M6

next_steps.action: Establish a structured, cross-functional innovation pipeline (e.g., quarterly ideation sprints)
Formalize the acquisition screening process and create a budget allocation model for diversification initiatives
Conduct an internal audit of current system integration gaps to improve operational efficiency

key_weaknesses: Lack of a formal, repeatable innovation process leading to inconsistent output.
High variability in execution velocity due to lack of executive sponsorship and clear resource allocation for non-core projects.
Poor integration between core ERP/CRM systems, hindering scalable growth and data-driven decision-making.
Reliance on isolated, grassroots efforts rather than a structured approach to strategic diversification.
